subject: home-economics
title: Food Studies Practical Coursework (Home Economics Scientific and Social), plus Textiles, Fashion and Design Elective Coursework (Elective 2 only)
weight: 20% (Food Studies); 10% (Textiles, Fashion and Design elective coursework, Elective 2 candidates only)
level: Common level (Higher and Ordinary sit the same assignments)
keyDates: Mon 2 November 2026 — Food Studies coursework completion date (SEC 2027 Food Studies Assignments and circular S61/25). Already passed.
6 November 2026 — Food Studies completion date given in SEC circular S68.2.26 (conflicts with 2 November; see conflicts). Already passed.
10 to 13 November 2026 — Schools Portal window for schools to upload Food Studies journals (S68.2.26). Already passed.
Before 23 October 2026 — deadline for schools to tell the SEC (practicals@examinations.ie) which candidates are doing the Textiles elective coursework (S61/25). Already passed.
Tuesday 6 April 2027 — Textiles, Fashion and Design elective coursework completion date (SEC 2027 brief and S61/25).
Textiles design folder and garment assessment/collection arrangements — TBC by SEC (the brief says schools will be notified).
June 2027 — written examination (SEC date TBC in the timetable).
summary: Food Studies is the practical journal: for each assignment you record an investigation, planning and preparation, implementation (a supervised practical) and evaluation in the SEC's digital Word booklet, which is converted to PDF and uploaded by your school. It is 20% of the subject, and for the 2027 cohort the completion date was 2 November 2026, so it should already be finished and submitted. If you take Elective 2 (Textiles, Fashion and Design) there is a second coursework, a design folder plus one made garment, worth 100 marks weighted to 10% of the subject, due on 6 April 2027.

stages.name: Choose and plan your assignments
stages.marksNote: Each Food Studies assignment is marked out of 80 (32 + 8 + 28 + 12). How many count is disputed between sources; see conflicts.

points: The SEC issued five assignments for 2027, common to Higher and Ordinary level: two in Area A (Application of Nutritional Principles), one in Area B (Food Preparation and Cooking Processes), one in Area D (Properties of a Food) and one in Area E (Comparative Analysis including Sensory Analysis). No Area C (Food Technology) assignment was set for 2027.

Assignment 1 (Area A) is about the challenges older people face in keeping a healthy diet, their nutritional needs and meal-planning guidelines, a range of two-course main-meal menus, and cooking one main course.

Assignment 2 (Area A) is about the causes and effects of iron deficiency, the nutritional needs and factors in planning meals to reduce the risk, a range of two-course main-meal menus, and cooking one main course.

Assignment 3 (Area B) is about commercially prepared filo and puff pastry: brands, forms, ingredients and cost, sweet and savoury dishes for each, the key points for success with the one you choose, and cooking one dish.
Assignment 4 (Area D) is about marinades: types of marinade and dishes that illustrate each, the benefits and principles of marinating, the key points for success, and cooking one marinated dish.

Assignment 5 (Area E) is about descriptive rating tests: their use in the food industry, researching commercial granola, choosing two brands with similar ingredients, agreeing six common sensory attributes, running the test with star diagrams and comparing the two sensory profiles.
The SEC's 2027 assignments document and circular S61/25 (October 2025) say candidates complete any four assignments.

The Department of Education's Assessment Arrangements 2027 (page 40), as summarised by ATHE, adjust this to two assignments from the five, and if you present more than two only the two highest-scoring are counted.
Do what your teacher tells you; your school will have followed whichever arrangement applies. Because the deadline has passed, this matters now only for understanding how your marks were counted.
A dish may be attempted only once. You cannot repeat a dish, or repeat it with small changes, in another assignment.
Pick dishes that fit the exact wording of the assignment and name them in the investigation, because the SEC requires dishes to be identified in the investigation.
Use fresh foods and avoid overusing convenience foods; the SEC says marks are lost if this is not met.
Practical work may be done in pairs, or in groups for Area E only. The written record must still be entirely your own.

checklistCandidates: Check the exact wording of each assignment before choosing dishes
Choose a different dish for every assignment
Name your chosen dishes in the investigation
Plan the practical with fresh foods, not convenience foods

stages.name: Investigation (analysis and research)
stages.marksNote: 32 marks per assignment, the largest single section.

guide.h: What the SEC recording criteria reward
points: Area A: investigate the nutritional needs of the group, identify and apply suitable meal-planning guidelines, suggest suitable or modified dishes, and give sources of information.
Area B: describe the food preparation process, skill or equipment, show you understand the key points for making a dish with it, suggest suitable dishes that illustrate it, and give sources.
Area C (not set in 2027): the method of processing and its principles, containers, packaging and labelling, suitable foods or dishes, and sources.
Area D: define the property, show understanding of the principles behind it, suggest dishes that illustrate it, and give sources.

Area E: investigate and describe the testing technique and its possible outcomes, investigate the foods or products to be tested, say which conditions must be controlled during the test, and give sources.
The criteria are to be read together with the specific wording of the assignment, so answer every command word in the brief (analyse, research, elaborate, discuss, suggest).

guide.h: Doing it well (what each 2027 brief asks for)
points: Older people (Assignment 1): analyse the challenges in keeping a healthy diet, then use them to justify your nutritional needs, meal-planning guidelines and menus.
Iron deficiency (Assignment 2): cover causes and effects separately, then link the planning factors in your research directly to the menus you suggest.

Pastry (Assignment 3): cover brands, forms available, ingredients and cost, and sweet and savoury dishes for both filo and puff, before choosing one. Teacher advice from StudyTok is to compare cost per 100 g as well as pack price.
Marinades (Assignment 4): cover several types of marinade with dishes for each, the benefits, the underlying principles, and the key points for success.
Granola (Assignment 5): cover the range of products with brands, ingredients, nutritional content and cost, then justify why the two chosen brands have similar ingredients.
Descriptive rating tests (Assignment 5): discuss how the food industry uses them, and plan the conditions to control so the test is fair (the SEC lists this under Area E).
The brief asks for a range of two-course menus (Assignments 1 and 2), so give several, not one, before picking a main course to cook.
Include a Sources of Information section in every investigation; the SEC lists sources under each area's criteria.

You must reference every source: books, journals, government reports, websites, other media, specialist organisations and individuals, and any material produced by AI software. Unreferenced material is treated as plagiarism.
Do not copy directly from sources apart from essential references such as definitions.
Tables, graphs, charts and diagrams are allowed. Label any you refer to as Figure 1, Figure 2 and so on. Images must not be used to smuggle in extra text, and videos are not allowed.
Do not include links to other material.

checklistCandidates: Answer every command word in the assignment brief
Cover each area's recording criteria in the investigation
Suggest a range of dishes or menus before choosing one
List every source, including any AI-generated material
Write the investigation in your own words
Label every table, chart or diagram as a Figure

stages.name: Planning and preparation

points: The journal page for this section has fields for the name of the dish or test, the source of the recipe, the date of the practical, and a table of ingredients or products with costs and the key equipment or testing equipment, ending in a total cost.
The SEC marks this section for resources: ingredients with quantities and costing, and key equipment. That is the whole criterion, so completeness and accuracy are what earn the marks.
Give exact quantities for every ingredient and a cost for each, then total them.
The dish must be the one identified in your investigation and must meet the assignment's requirements.
List all the key equipment you will use, including testing equipment for Area E.

Teacher advice (StudyTok) adds a time plan with timings and pre-preparation steps and critical control points; the SEC criterion does not require these as separate headings, so treat them as optional extras that also support your implementation write-up.
Record the real date of the practical; practical work must be done in class time under your teacher's supervision.

checklistCandidates: Fill in the dish name, recipe source and practical date
Give an exact quantity for every ingredient
Cost each ingredient and add up the total
List all key equipment, including testing equipment for Area E

stages.name: Implementation (the supervised practical)

points: All practical work must be done in class time under the supervision of your Home Economics teacher. A teacher demonstration does not count.
You may cook in pairs, or in groups for Area E, but your written account must be your own.

Cook, and serve, one dish from your research, as the assignment states: a main course for Assignments 1 and 2, one pastry dish for Assignment 3, one marinated dish for Assignment 4, and for Assignment 5 the descriptive rating test on two granolas.
An outline of the procedure you followed during the practical, including the food preparation processes or testing procedures used.
The key factors you considered when making the dish or running the test.
Safety and hygiene issues relevant to the dish, foods or test.
Teacher advice (StudyTok) is to be specific: give cutting sizes, hygiene steps, storage temperatures and why you made each adjustment, instead of a one-line summary.

Marinade (Assignment 4): the brief asks you to follow key points for success; StudyTok lists avoiding metal containers and not reusing raw marinade on cooked food as hygiene and technique points. Treat these as teacher advice, not SEC rules.
Pastry (Assignment 3): StudyTok advises against egg-washing cut edges of puff pastry, which glues the layers; again teacher advice.
Sensory test (Assignment 5): use the same six agreed attributes for both products, record results on star diagrams, and compile a sensory profile for each product.
Write up while the details are fresh; Study Skills Ireland says reconstructed entries written weeks later are easy to spot and lose marks.

checklistCandidates: Do the practical in class under your teacher's supervision
Outline the procedure step by step
State the key factors you considered
Record safety and hygiene points for this dish or test
Write up the practical soon after doing it
Use the same six attributes for both granolas on star diagrams

stages.name: Evaluation

guide.h: Two parts, set by the SEC
points: Every 2027 brief asks you to evaluate in terms of (a) implementation and (b) a specific requirement of that assignment; the journal repeats this as evaluation of implementation and of the specific requirements of the assignment.
Assignments 1 and 2: part (b) is the specific requirements of the assignment.
Assignment 3: part (b) is the advantages and/or disadvantages of using your chosen pastry when baking and cooking at home.
Assignment 4: part (b) is the success of the marinade in achieving its intended purpose or purposes.
Assignment 5: part (b) is the test results, meaning the comparison of the two sensory profiles.
Keep (a) and (b) as separate, clearly headed parts; StudyTok lists merging them as a common mistake.
Judge, then give evidence from what actually happened in your practical, then say what you would change.
In (a), cover how the practical went: time management, hygiene, skills, and the quality of the finished dish.

The 2006 to 2007 Inspectorate report on Home Economics found students needed more guidance and practice in evaluation and critical appraisal; that report is older, but it is one of the few official comments on this skill.
For Assignment 5, remember a descriptive test measures how strongly each attribute is present, not personal liking (StudyTok advice).

checklistCandidates: Write evaluation (a) on implementation under its own heading
Write evaluation (b) on the specific requirement under its own heading
Support every judgement with evidence from your practical
Say what you would change next time

stages.name: Finalise, convert and submit the journal
stages.marksNote: No separate marks, but work that is not visible cannot be marked.

points: Complete everything in the SEC's 2027 digital Food Studies Coursework Journal, supplied as a Word (.docx) file; you may not change its structure or format.
Put your examination number and date of birth on the cover.
Record the area of practice and assignment number for each assignment.
Formatting in the 2027 journal: Arial, size 12, 1.5 line spacing; margins 20 mm left, right and top and 30 mm at the bottom; type only in the bracketed entry areas.
Text can overflow a box and vanish, particularly if pasted in. The SEC states that anything not visible will not be marked.
Convert the finished booklet to PDF, print the final PDF and proofread the printout to check all your work is visible.
Give the printed copy to your teacher; the school keeps the printed and digital versions until appeals are over.
When you sign the P.2 authentication form you confirm the printed copy matches what is uploaded.
The school uploads the PDF through the Schools Portal; the file name format is 2027-098-2-EV-(your exam number).pdf for English.
Back up your journal securely until the SEC has received it.

checklistCandidates: Put your exam number and date of birth on the cover
Keep Arial 12, 1.5 spacing and the booklet margins
Check no text has overflowed or disappeared in any box
Convert to PDF and proofread the printed copy
Sign the P.2 form only after checking the printout

stages.name: Elective 2 only: design folder (25 marks)
stages.marksNote: Part of the 100-mark Textiles coursework (design folder 25 + garment 75), weighted to 10% of the subject. Elective 2 candidates only.

points: Theme: values, interests and personality expressed through a holiday wardrobe.
Task: design and sketch an outfit suitable for a young person to wear on holiday, set out the design specifications, then make and evaluate one garment from it.
The outfit can be knitted, crocheted or machine stitched.
The garment must include two of three processes: button/s and buttonhole/s; darts or shaping; pocket.
You must follow the design process and present a design folder with analysis and research, implementation and evaluation.

Design brief, analysis and research (15 marks): analyse the brief to identify key requirements and constraints, explore the theme, describe the proposed outfit with design sketches having regard to the theme and mandatory processes, justify the outfit and the garment to be made, and outline the planned course of action.
Implementation (4 marks): the work sequence you followed, with brief reference to how you carried out the mandatory processes.
Evaluation (6 marks): evaluate the garment, the difficulties met and how they were addressed, and proposed modifications; also evaluate the outcomes in relation to the brief.
Individual work only; group work is not acceptable.
All work is done under your teacher's supervision and every source, including AI-generated material, is referenced.
Put your examination number on the folder and on the garment.

checklistCandidates: List the brief's key requirements and constraints
Explore the holiday theme and show it in your sketches
Justify the outfit and the garment you chose to make
Record the work sequence and how you did each mandatory process
Evaluate the garment against the brief and note modifications

stages.name: Elective 2 only: the garment (75 marks) and submission
stages.marksNote: 75 marks: design aspects 15, skills and processes 50, finish 10. Completion date 6 April 2027.

points: Design aspects (15): the garment suits the brief, applies design principles, shows aesthetic consideration and creativity.
Skills and processes (50): use of materials, equipment and skills, and execution of the prescribed processes. This is two thirds of the garment marks.
Finish (10): presentation of the completed garment.

It must be textile based, include the specified processes, show a clearly identifiable interpretation of the theme, and show competence in a range of textile skills that progress from Junior Cycle Home Economics.
Make one garment from the outfit you designed.
The completion date is Tuesday 6 April 2027. The SEC says arrangements for assessing the folder and garment, and the dates, will be notified to schools.
The SEC circular says the school must have notified it before 23 October 2026 that you are doing the Textiles coursework.
If you submit the Textiles coursework you sit a written exam weighted 70%, Food Studies is 20%, and the Textiles coursework is 10%.

A 2025 marking scheme noted that candidates who submitted the Textiles coursework may attempt only Elective Question 2; check the 2027 paper instructions as this was reported by a search summary, not read in full.

checklistCandidates: Include two of the three mandatory processes in the garment
Make the theme clearly visible in the design
Show a range of textile skills beyond Junior Cycle level
Finish and press the garment for presentation
Put your exam number on the garment and folder

criteria.name: Food Studies: Investigation (analysis and research)
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Covers every point set for the assignment's area of practice, answers every command word in the brief, suggests a suitable range of dishes or menus, and cites all sources. The SEC publishes the criteria only as headings, so no further mark breakdown is available.

criteria.name: Food Studies: Planning and Preparation
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Accurate ingredient list with quantities and costs, a total cost, and a full list of key equipment.

criteria.name: Food Studies: Implementation
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: A clear outline of the procedure actually followed, the key factors considered, and safety and hygiene issues relevant to the dish, food or test.

criteria.name: Food Studies: Evaluation
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Separate evaluation of the implementation and of the assignment's specific requirement, with evidence from your own practical.

criteria.name: Textiles design folder: analysis and research
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Analysis of the brief with requirements and constraints, theme exploration, described and sketched outfit, justification, and a planned course of action.

criteria.name: Textiles design folder: implementation
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Work sequence with brief reference to how the mandatory processes were carried out.

criteria.name: Textiles design folder: evaluation
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Evaluates the garment, difficulties and how they were addressed, proposed modifications, and outcomes in relation to the brief.

criteria.name: Textiles garment: design aspects
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Garment appropriate to the brief, application of design principles, aesthetic considerations and creativity.

criteria.name: Textiles garment: skills and processes
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Skilled use of materials, equipment and techniques, and correct execution of the prescribed processes.

rules: All practical work and journal writing must be done in class time under your Home Economics teacher's supervision; teacher demonstration does not count. If it is not supervised, the work cannot be validated and will not be credited.
A dish may be attempted only once; repeating or partly changing and repeating it in another assignment loses marks.
Dishes must meet the assignment's requirements and be identified in the investigation; use fresh foods and avoid overusing convenience foods or you lose marks.
Practical work may be in pairs, or groups for Area E only, but the written record must be your own. Evidence of collaboration in the recording means the assignment's marks are disallowed.
Reference all sources, including anything produced by AI. Unreferenced material counts as plagiarism, and penalties range up to losing the subject or being debarred.
Do not change the booklet's structure, format or margins; use Arial 12 with 1.5 line spacing, no extra links, and no videos.
Text that is not visible in the printed PDF cannot earn marks, so proofread the printout.
Bonus marks are not given for coursework completed through Irish.
Textiles coursework: individual work only, textile based, includes the specified processes, examination number on the folder and garment, and supervised by your teacher.
mistakes: Writing journal entries weeks after the practical from memory, which Study Skills Ireland says is easy for examiners to spot (teacher-site claim).
Pasting text into a box so part of it overflows and disappears from the printed PDF, so it cannot be marked (SEC warning).
Repeating or lightly changing a dish across assignments (SEC: marks lost).
Relying on convenience foods instead of fresh foods (SEC: marks lost).
Merging the two parts of the evaluation into one narrative (StudyTok).
Treating the Area E sensory test as a measure of personal preference rather than rating attribute intensity (StudyTok).
Leaving out citations or a sources section (SEC lists sources under every area; StudyTok).
Copying definitions or text from sources or from classmates; collaboration in the written record disallows the marks (SEC).
Not being familiar with the assessment criteria in the journal; the Inspectorate's 2006 to 2007 report noted this in some journals, and found students needed more practice in evaluation.

conflicts: Number of Food Studies assignments: the SEC's 2027 assignments document and circular S61/25 (October 2025) say candidates complete any four, but the Department's Assessment Arrangements 2027 and ATHE say two of the five, with the best two counted. The app's hom-cooking-methods-s7.json says two of five, so it matches the Department's later adjustment but not the SEC documents. I could not confirm which version your school applied.

Food Studies completion date: SEC assignments document and S61/25 say 2 November 2026, but circular S68.2.26 lists 6 November 2026 with a portal window of 10 to 13 November 2026. Either way the date has passed. The app does not state this date.

Textiles mandatory processes: the SEC 2027 brief says the garment must include two of three processes, but the Department's Assessment Arrangements 2027 says an adjustment requires one mandatory process from three. The app (hom-clothing-selection-s5.json) says two of three, matching the SEC brief. Check with your teacher which applies.

Marks per assignment versus 20%: each assignment is marked out of 80 and the journal has four assignment sections, but no source I read explains how these marks are scaled into the 20% of the subject, so the total mark value is left as null.

The app says the Food Studies marks are Investigation 32, Planning 8, Implementation 28, Evaluation 12; this matches the journal. The app also says dishes cannot be repeated and that fresh foods should be used; this matches the SEC.
No Chief Examiner's report on the Food Studies coursework was found; the 'mistakes' come from SEC warnings, an old Inspectorate report and teacher sites, and teacher-site items are not official.
Journal formatting differs between years: the 2025 journal gave a bottom margin of 35 mm and no line spacing; the 2027 journal gives 30 mm and 1.5 line spacing. The 2027 figures are used here.
